text:
Alex Ovechkin's final season has become a tour of goodbyes. The Lightning gave him custom "hot stick" cigars before his last game in Tampa on Tuesday, as NHL.com reported, and he told his teammates in October that this would be his last year. What it hasn't had is goals.

He has one in 19 games. Tuesday made it 14 straight without one, which Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted matches the longest drought of his career, from late 2023. Our numbers say he's due: one goal on 5.3 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and over his last ten games he has generated more than his usual rate, 3.5 expected goals against 2.7. His hardest shot this season still ranks in the 97th percentile.

The legs are another matter. He's 41, playing under 14 minutes a night, and his top skating speed sits at the bottom of the league. Last season Evolving-Hockey had his results running ahead of his chances; this season it's the reverse. Goals tend to follow chances, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the league's best at getting to the front of the net last season. That part hasn't left him.
